title: Direct Connect with a Site-to-Site VPN backup
claim: One transit gateway connects the data center to both VPCs over Direct Connect, with a Site-to-Site VPN connection as the backup.
alt: A corporate data center at the top holds a customer gateway device. Two paths lead down from it to one transit gateway in an AWS Region. The primary path is highlighted and runs through AWS Direct Connect and a Direct Connect gateway. The backup path is dashed and runs through the internet and an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection. Below the transit gateway are EC2 instances in VPC A and in VPC B, and the transit gateway connects to both VPCs.
notes: Pilot diagram, the wide stress case. Round 1 was five columns from left to right (806 units): clean on a desktop, but it scrolled sideways on a phone and hid the transit gateway. From round 2 the same content is two columns from top to bottom. The topology comes from memory and must be grounded in the fact canon before the figure is used in a chapter. No speeds, limits or counts are drawn. The Region is named in the alt text only, because one Region box is a lint error. Wide variants: _build/tmp/pilot-lab/diagrams/src/pilot-hybrid-wide*.json.

edges.label: primary
edges.say: The customer gateway device sends traffic for AWS over the Direct Connect connection, which is the primary path.
The Direct Connect connection carries the traffic to a Direct Connect gateway.
The Direct Connect gateway passes the traffic to the transit gateway.
The transit gateway routes the traffic to VPC A or VPC B through a VPC attachment.

edges.label: backup
edges.say: If Direct Connect fails, the customer gateway device sends the traffic over the internet, which is the backup path.
On the internet, the traffic travels inside a Site-to-Site VPN connection.
The Site-to-Site VPN connection ends on the same transit gateway.
